name: genotyping
_why_schema_version: Mandatory. With {frz}/{new} expansion, @-over-callers and a second module in flight, a reader must be able to tell a stale reader from a stale file. A version this build does not implement is a refusal, never a best-effort parse.
_why_callers: The callers that produced output in this cohort. Each `@` key in the steps expands over this list.
_why_unused_callers: dragen and melt produced no output in this cohort. Upstream binds their VCFs and declares their per-caller outputs on steps 06-08; those inputs are optional (`File?`) and the WDLs collect caller VCFs with select_all, so leaving them unbound drops nothing.

freeze._why_attrs: What steps 06/07 consume from upstream: the ClusterBatch and GatherBatchEvidence outputs plus median_cov. Steps 07-10 read each other's new outputs, which are produced inside the sandbox, so they are not frozen. The index attributes are listed because they are separate objects on the row that must sit next to their VCFs in the sandbox bucket.
freeze._why_attr_suffix: The chain's steps read `this.<attr>{frz}`, written beside the baseline's own attribute on the cloned batch row, so the unsuffixed name keeps pointing at the baseline object.
freeze._why_row_mode: The batch sample_set already exists in the sandbox (it is cloned with the workspace); attrs only adds the frozen attributes to it.
freeze._why_tag: Empty: this module keeps the unsuffixed names it has always used (manifests/baseline_frozen_inputs.json, staging/frozen_baseline_attrs.tsv, gs://<sandbox bucket>/frozen-baseline/), which docs/terra-head-to-head.md and existing work trees refer to.

steps._why_FilterBatchSites.N_IQR_cutoff_plott: the value is the STRING "6" (and step 08's "10000"), because that is what this map has always posted and what Rawls accepted. Rule 3 says a literal carries its real type; the type recorded here is the one on the wire. Changing it to a JSON number changes the bytes of the POST, so it is not a refactor and does not belong in this file.

steps._why_FilterBatchSamples.N_IQR_cutoff: the value is the STRING "6" (and step 08's "10000"), because that is what this map has always posted and what Rawls accepted. Rule 3 says a literal carries its real type; the type recorded here is the one on the wire. Changing it to a JSON number changes the bytes of the POST, so it is not a refactor and does not belong in this file.

steps._why_entity_row: The row this step runs against is a COHORT (a sample_set_set), and no key in kit/gsvtk-config holds one: GSVTK_BATCH names a sample_set, so the configured batch row is the wrong KIND here, not merely the wrong value. Stated as `--entity` rather than left out so the answer is in the file: the operator names the row -- the one the 09-* submissions `batch_status.py` lists were made against -- and `terra/batch_rerun_step.py` refuses `--step 09 submit` rather than guess it. Guessing submits a row that is not a cohort, every `this.*` input binds to nothing, and the submission still reports itself accepted (docs/terra-head-to-head.md).

steps._why_GenotypeBatch.training_vcf: branch-only: main trains PE/SR from `vcf`, the branch from a separate batch VCF. Both are coherent pipelines; they are different pipelines. Dropping it is a semantic change, not a fix. main's GenotypeBatch declares 21 inputs (18 + 3 dockers); the branch declares 26, adding training_vcf, genotype_args, training_args, n_RD_genotype_bins and fail_on_degenerate_sr_cutoffs. This map binds only training_vcf -- the other four have WDL defaults -- so it is the single key a main-shaped run has to drop. It was posted against a main-derived ref and rejected as an extra input; that is what happened, and this field is why `check` can name it instead of just failing.
steps._why_unbound: n_RD_genotype_bins (100000) and fail_on_degenerate_sr_cutoffs (true) come from the WDL defaults - the point of the branch is that these are now correct by default.
steps._why_branch_only_outputs: The branch's trainer writes separate depth and PE/SR copy-number tables, plus a diagnostics table for the SR cutoffs; upstream declares none of them.
steps._why_upstream_only_outputs: Upstream's single RD table, which the branch replaces with genotyping_rd_depth_table and genotyping_rd_pesr_table.
steps._why_export: The new-side attributes terra/batch_fetch_compare.sh fetches off the entity once the chain finishes, as data rather than as shell literals (docs/module-profiles.md). These 7 are NOT derived from `outputs` and the loader deliberately does not compare the two: this step WRITES 10 attributes, 8 once the `_index` siblings are excluded, and the script demanded 7 of those 8, carrying the eighth -- regeno_coverage_medians -- as optional. Promoting that eighth name was asked and REJECTED: `required` is the script's exit code, so a required attribute that some chain never wrote turns every such baseline into a fetch that exits 1 where it passes today -- a product decision with a money-path consequence, to be taken with a real run in hand, not smuggled inside a refactor. `scripts/selftest.d/profiles.sh`'s export-list guard pins these 7 against `outputs`, states the 7-vs-8 delta as a fact, and carries the positive control that edits THIS field to prove the shell follows the data rather than a literal.
